subject: Sequenced acceptance & signing lanes — MAP + MSA/DPA/order-form dependencies
messages:

Cc: ravi.menon@medalignhealth.com

Subject: MAP + legal gating questions for Redwood pilot

Irene,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency profiles. Procurement asked me to pull together the actual sequencing we need to get to a signed order form + MSA/DPA in Q1. A few things they want clarified before we build a formal MAP: 

- Which documents must be signed before we can start the pilot (MSA vs. Order Form)?
- Are there any DPA items that require a separate SLA addendum or can they be appended to the MSA?
- Typical internal lead times for legal review at Redwood for redlines / counter-signature?

I sketched a rough timeline but would prefer Redwood to propose the critical path. Can you also share your MAP template and a simple deliverables checklist so our legal and IT security folks can map dependencies on their side.

Attached: none (I will share our procurement intake once we align).

- Elaine

From: irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
To: Elaine Tucker <elaine.tucker@medalignhealth.com>, Sara Holt <procurement@medalignhealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 4 Dec 2025 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP + legal gating questions for Redwood pilot

Hi Elaine / Sara — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a concise sequenced plan and attached a draft MAP that maps each legal/IT/ops checkpoint to acceptance gates. High level:

1) Pilot kickoff (can start after Order Form signature and basic DPA terms agreed in principle).
   - We normally require a signed Order Form for billing + initial capacity reservation.
   - MSA signature is required before production data ingestion or dedicated private deployment. For a hosted pilot (no PHI), we can proceed with the Order Form + a short-term DPA SSC (standard scoping) while MSA redlines progress in parallel.

2) DPA handling:
   - Most customers choose to incorporate DPA language in the MSA exhibit; if you have specific data residency/KMS requirements we’ll add an addendum.
   - If you need an external HSM/KMS integration, that will be a separate SOW and typically pushes the onramp 3–6 weeks.

3) Legal turnaround:
   - Typical first-redline turnaround from Redwood legal is 3–5 business days for standard requests. Complex security controls or gov/regulatory language can extend to 10–14 business days.

Next steps I propose (short checklist):
- We (Redwood) send a draft MAP + Order Form outline (attached). [Attachment: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx]
- MedAlign legal flags any must-have redlines on the MSA and any DPA exhibits within 5 business days.
- If procurement needs an internal approval checklist, share it and we’ll align owners on our side.

I’ve cc’d Jonas (legal ops) and Vanessa (customer success/runbook) to provide timing commitments and operational requirements.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the milestones. Proposed times: 10:00–11:00 PT or 13:00–14:00 PT.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Programs, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference — Making inference predictable

From: Sara Holt <procurement@medalignhealth.com>
To: irene_choi@redwoodinference.com, Elaine Tucker <elaine.tucker@medalignhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Dec 2025 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MAP + legal gating questions for Redwood pilot

Irene — appreciate the clear breakdown. A couple clarifications from procurement/legal POV: 

- MedAlign requires the MSA signed before any vendor can access production data. Our pilot will be limited to synthetic/non-PHI datasets unless the MSA+DPA are fully executed.
- We prefer that the DPA be a stand-alone exhibit for auditability. If Redwood can accept that, it will help our internal auditors.
- Our internal SLA/Procurement cadence: once we have Redwood’s redlined MSA back, we usually need 7 business days for internal legal review; procurement needs an additional 3 business days for PO processing once the Order Form is signed.

We received the MAP and have one initial redline request on the MSA: section 8.2 (data deletion retention) — see attached redlines. We’ll follow up with a DocuSign package for easy countersignature once we exchange final templates.

Also sending our internal approval checklist as a separate attachment to this thread (not included here).

Thanks — Sara
Sara Holt
Senior Procurement Manager, MedAlign Health
procurement@medalignhealth.com

Elaine / Sara — thanks for the quick turnaround and the redlines. We reviewed section 8.2 and submitted a counterproposal that maintains your auditability concerns while keeping our standard retention workflow. I attached the redlined MSA with our comments.

Condensed critical path (proposed, with dates assuming we start next week):
- Dec 8: Redwood returns MSA counter-redlines (done) & updated Order Form v0.3 (attached) — action: Redwood legal / Sales Ops
- Dec 9–19: MedAlign legal review (7 business days) — action: MedAlign legal
- Dec 20: Final sign execution via DocuSign (MSA + DPA exhibit + Order Form) — action: signatories
- Jan 5: Pilot begins (2-week pilot plan attached to MAP) — action: CS & MedAlign ops

Operational clarifications we need from MedAlign before Dec 9:
- Confirm whether pilot will use synthetic data or require private VPC (affects DPA scope).
- If KMS/HSM integration is required, mark as "out-of-scope" for initial pilot in the MAP and we’ll schedule a separate SOW.

Attach: OrderForm_Draft_v0.3.docx, MSA_redlines_20251205.pdf

If the timeline above looks OK, I’ll create a short mutual action plan (Milestone worksheet) in HubSpot and share the DocuSign envelope link once we get sign-off on the counters.
